title: Lexeme timing ledger and cache chargeback instrumentation
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Add instrumentation and end-to-end pipeline to record per-lexeme (token) timing and cache impact, produce a "ledger" per request that allows cost chargeback and latency attribution down to the lexeme level without overwhelming cardinality. This will power new dashboards for latency/error decomposition and a chargeback signal for Dedicated billing and cost-optimizations in Optimize.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a compact lexeme-timing event for every emitted lexeme (sampled by configurable rate) with fields: model, shard_id, request_id, seq_pos, is_prompt, kv_cache_hit, kernel, kernel_ms, emission_ms
Events are exported to our OTLP collector and appear in the telemetry pipeline with agreed schema
A downstream aggregator produces a per-request ledger that summarizes tokens, cache-hit ratio, total extra compute attributed to cache misses, and per-lexeme p95/p99 timings
End-to-end P50/P95 latency attribution dashboard created in Grafana with filters for model, region, route, and cache-hit buckets
Sampling knobs and cardinality controls exist and the end-to-end CPU/memory overhead on the runtime is <2% at typical load
Integration test and a small dedicated canary run validate correctness and overhead before wider rollout
tasks: Design compact telemetry schema: field names, enums, sampling metadata, and stable schema version
Add runtime hooks in emission path to write lexeme timing events (C++/Rust instrument) with minimal allocations
Implement adaptive sampler (slow-path store for extreme sequences) and config matrix for canary burn-in
Extend OTLP exporter to tag lexeme events and route to 'telemetry-lexeme' topic in Kafka
Build aggregator service (consumer) to assemble per-request ledgers and compute cache-miss chargebacks
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules for regression (latency per-lexeme and cache-chargeback increases)
Add end-to-end tests that inject synthetic cache-hit/miss patterns and validate ledger arithmetic
Run 1-week canary in staging with traffic mirroring and budgeted sampling rates
notes: We use the word 'lexeme' in this ticket to avoid confusion with existing token telemetry and to signal the compact schema (lexeme-level is equivalent to token/wordpiece for our instrumentation).
Primary risk is cardinality explosion. Mitigations: sampling, compact enums, avoid attaching freeform prompts in events, and use per-request ledger assembly rather than long-lived per-lexeme traces.

Cache-chargeback calculation approach: attribute additional kernel_ms observed on cache-miss emissions to the lexeme that experienced the miss; aggregate per-request as a sum of extra_ms over baseline kernel_ms for hits. We'll validate baseline per-model in a short profiling job.
Privacy: ensure no prompt text is exported with lexeme events; only indices/flags and safe enums are allowed in the schema.
Operational plan: start with sampling=0.02 (2%) globally, 1.0 for selected internal tenants; iterate based on telemetry volume and dashboard usefulness.
